# Singapore Dinner Fit for 4: Thai vs Japanese

For a group of 4 with one vegetarian and one gluten-free diner, **Restaurant A (Thai, casual, small plates)** is the better fit overall. It is usually easier to mix-and-match dishes for different diets and stay within **SGD 35 per person**.

# Best Choice for Your Group

| Option | Fit for group | Diet flexibility | Budget fit | Dinner vibe | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Restaurant A | Strong | High | Good | Social, casual | Can get noisy; gluten-free needs careful ordering |
| Restaurant B | Moderate | Medium | Good | Quieter, structured | Set meals may limit vegetarian and gluten-free choices |

**Why Restaurant A wins**
- Thai menus often have more **vegetarian-friendly** dishes and shared plates.
- Small plates make it easier to build a meal around the gluten-free diner’s needs.
- Casual settings work well for groups of 4 and shared ordering.
- Staying under **SGD 35 each** is more realistic when you can split several lower-cost dishes.

**Restaurant A — Pros**
- Many small plates, so the group can share and customize.
- Better chance of finding multiple vegetarian options.
- Easier to avoid gluten if dishes can be ordered without soy-heavy sauces or fried coatings.
- Good for a relaxed group dinner.

**Restaurant A — Cons**
- Gluten-free safety depends on sauce ingredients, cross-contact, and fryer use.
- Small-plate dining can add up if the group orders many items.
- Casual atmosphere may be louder and less intimate.

**Restaurant B — Pros**
- Quieter environment, which may suit a calmer dinner.
- Set meals can make ordering simpler and more predictable.
- Japanese cuisine can offer some naturally gluten-free items if chosen carefully.

**Restaurant B — Cons**
- Set meals are often less flexible for one vegetarian and one gluten-free diner at the same table.
- Some Japanese dishes rely on soy sauce, batter, or shared broths that may contain gluten.
- The group may have fewer easy “everyone can eat this” options.

# Quick Recommendation

- **Choose Restaurant A** if your top priority is **group flexibility, sharing, and easier accommodation of both dietary needs**.
- **Choose Restaurant B** only if the group strongly prefers a **quieter setting** and you can confirm vegetarian and gluten-free set options in advance.
